# Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM Provider

Terraform provider for Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM

## Resources

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`uem_profile`](resources/profile.md) | Manages a Workspace ONE UEM Profile (Android, Apple iOS, AppleOsX, Windows 10, Windows_Rugged, or Linux) |
| [`uem_mac_application`](resources/mac_application.md) | Uploads a macOS application to Workspace ONE UEM |
| [`uem_application_assignment`](resources/application_assignment.md) | Manages a Workspace ONE UEM Application Assignment |
| [`uem_purchased_application_assignment`](resources/purchased_application_assignment.md) | Manages assignment rules for a purchased (VPP) Apple application by UUID |
| [`uem_mac_script`](resources/mac_script.md) | Manages a macOS script in Workspace ONE UEM |
| [`uem_script_assignment`](resources/script_assignment.md) | Manages script assignments for a Workspace ONE UEM script |
| [`uem_mac_sensor`](resources/mac_sensor.md) | Manages a macOS device sensor in Workspace ONE UEM (MDM API V2) |
| [`uem_sensor_assignment`](resources/sensor_assignment.md) | Manages device sensor assignments for a Workspace ONE UEM sensor (MDM API V2) |
| [`uem_update_deployment`](resources/update_deployment.md) | Manages a device update deployment in Workspace ONE UEM (MDM Updates API v1) |
| [`uem_smart_group`](resources/smart_group.md) | Manages a smart group in Workspace ONE UEM (MDM API v1) |

## Data Sources

| Data Source | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`uem_profiles`](data-sources/profiles.md) | Searches for profiles by platform and organization group |

| [`uem_sensors`](data-sources/sensors.md) | Searches for macOS device sensors within an organization group |
| [`uem_update_deployments`](data-sources/update_deployments.md) | Enumerates device update deployments across the update catalog |
| [`uem_smart_groups`](data-sources/smart_groups.md) | Looks up smart groups by id, UUID, name, or organization group |
| [`uem_organization_groups`](data-sources/organization_groups.md) | Looks up organization groups by search, id, parent, or ancestry |

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example Workspace ONE UEM Provider Configuration

# This provider is not yet published to the Terraform Registry; install it
# from the pre-release mirror zip (see the project README) before running
# `terraform init`. For local development against a source build, see
# "Developing the provider locally" in the README for the dev_overrides
# workflow, which skips `terraform init` entirely.
terraform {
  required_providers {
    uem = {
      source = "registry.terraform.io/omnissa/uem"
    }
  }
}

# Provider configuration using environment variables
# Set these in your .env file or export them before running terraform
provider "uem" {
  # All configuration can be provided via environment variables:
  # - UEM_INSTANCE_URL
  # - UEM_TENANT_CODE
  # - UEM_AUTH_METHOD (basic or oauth2)
  # - UEM_USERNAME (for basic auth)
  # - UEM_PASSWORD (for basic auth)
  # - UEM_CLIENT_ID (for oauth2)
  # - UEM_CLIENT_SECRET (for oauth2)
  # - UEM_OAUTH2_TOKEN_URL (for oauth2)

  # Or you can specify them explicitly:
  # instance_url = "https://your-instance.awmdm.com"
  # tenant_code  = "your-tenant-code"
  # auth_method  = "basic"  # optional — inferred from configured credentials when unset
  # username     = "admin-username"
  # password     = "admin-password"
}

# Example using Basic Auth explicitly
# provider "uem" {
#   instance_url = "https://cn1234.awmdm.com"
#   tenant_code  = "YourTenantCode"
#   auth_method  = "basic"
#   username     = "admin@example.com"
#   password     = "your-password"
# }

# Example using OAuth2 explicitly
# provider "uem" {
#   instance_url    = "https://cn1234.awmdm.com"
#   tenant_code     = "YourTenantCode"
#   auth_method     = "oauth2"
#   client_id       = "your-client-id"
#   client_secret   = "your-client-secret"
#   oauth2_token_url = "https://na.uemauth.workspaceone.com/connect/token"
# }
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `app_binary_storage_path` (String) Local directory where uem_mac_application binaries (DMG/plist) are stored for read/import round-tripping. Can also be set via UEM_APP_BINARY_DIR environment variable. Defaults to uem-artifacts/app-binaries (relative to the Terraform working directory) if unset — never a home directory.
- `auth_method` (String) Authentication method: 'basic' or 'oauth2'. Optional — can also be set via the UEM_AUTH_METHOD environment variable. When left unset, the provider infers the method from whichever credential set(s) are configured: oauth2 is preferred when both username+password and client_id+client_secret are complete; otherwise whichever single set is complete is used. When explicitly set (config or env), the explicit value wins and the corresponding credential set must be present or Configure fails. Both credential sets may be supplied simultaneously; only the resolved/primary method's client is used for resource and data source calls.
- `client_id` (String) Client ID for OAuth2 Authentication. Can also be set via UEM_CLIENT_ID environment variable.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client Secret for OAuth2 Authentication. Can also be set via UEM_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable.
- `instance_url` (String) Workspace ONE UEM instance URL (e.g., https://your-instance.awmdm.com). Can also be set via UEM_INSTANCE_URL environment variable.
- `oauth2_token_url` (String) OAuth2 token URL. Defaults to https://na.uemauth.workspaceone.com/connect/token. Can also be set via UEM_OAUTH2_TOKEN_URL environment variable.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for Basic Authentication. Can also be set via UEM_PASSWORD environment variable.
- `tenant_code` (String, Sensitive) Workspace ONE UEM tenant code (API Key). Can also be set via UEM_TENANT_CODE environment variable.
- `username` (String) Username for Basic Authentication. Can also be set via UEM_USERNAME environment variable.

## Environment Variables (operational, not provider configuration)

These are not provider schema attributes and cannot be set in a `provider "uem" {}` block; they tune the HTTP client's timeouts for every request the provider makes, and are read once at provider start.

- `UEM_HTTP_HEADER_TIMEOUT` — how long the provider waits for a server to start sending a response's headers before giving up (a Go duration string, e.g. `"90s"`, `"2m"`). Defaults to `60s`. An empty/unset value uses the default; an invalid value (not a Go duration, or non-positive) also falls back to the default and logs a warning.
- `UEM_HTTP_STALL_TIMEOUT` — how long the provider will wait for more data while reading a response body before treating the connection as stalled and failing (same format/default/fallback behavior as above). This is what allows a `uem_mac_application` import to download a large, slow-but-healthy application binary without an arbitrary overall timeout: only a genuine gap in the data (no bytes for this long) fails the download, with a diagnostic naming how many bytes were transferred and how many are expected (when known). It does not need to be raised for a larger file — only for a slower network path to UEM than the default 60s idle window tolerates.
